extracted.intended_audience: chemical manufacturers, importers, distributors, label and SDS preparers, workplace safety professionals, and commenters on OSHA rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and finalized decisions on wording, conditional instructions, and placement of precautionary statements in Appendix C of the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HCS) to align with GHS Rev. 7 and implement label/SDS requirements. Covers PPE wording, ignition-source language, storage/handling instructions, response phrases, and related editorial changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No hearing protection for certain hazard classes
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA will not add the term “hearing protection” for the hazard classes of germ cell mutagenicity (C.4.8), carcinogenicity (C.4.9), and reproductive toxicity (C.4.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: hearing protection does not protect against these hazardous substances and would be inappropriate; label and SDS preparers are not expected to include it for these hazard classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labelers may add PPE beyond table options
rubrics_metrics.description: Although OSHA did not adopt NIOSH's suggested PPE additions for some hazard classes, label preparers can add additional statements they deem appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA considered NIOSH recommendations out of scope but finalized ellipses at ends of PPE lists to allow adding other types of PPE (including respiratory protection) if appropriate for the chemical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses permit additional PPE (including respiratory protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA finalized ellipses at the end of PPE lists in prevention columns to allow addition of other types of PPE (including respiratory protection) where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although OSHA did not directly add 'respiratory protection' to certain hazard classes, the ellipses provide flexibility for label preparers to include respiratory protection when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not strengthen duty phrasing for preparer (avoid 'as required')
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA declined Cal/OSHA's suggested change to the precautionary statement wording that would add 'as required' to the duty of the label preparer to specify PPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA considers existing declarative statements (e.g., 'Wear protective gloves/...') sufficiently clear about required PPE; changing to 'as required' would not add strength and would only alter the duty phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory good practices not added if outside NPRM scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions like 'Mouth pipetting is to be prohibited. When pipetting is required, use a pipette bulb or a mechanical device' (for Aspiration Hazard C.4.13) were not adopted because they were not in the NPRM and are not in the GHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA notes laboratory-specific standards (29 CFR 1910.1450 Appendix A) already provide relevant procedures (e.g., 'Pipetting should never be done by mouth'). Label changes will not replicate out-of-scope lab practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contact during pregnancy and while nursing (explicit inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Change phrasing from 'during pregnancy/while nursing' to 'during pregnancy and while nursing' for reproductive toxicity (C.4.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label preparers must include both scenarios (pregnancy and nursing) and not choose between them; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete 'do not handle until all safety precautions read' for unstable explosives
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA deleted the 2012 HCS statement 'Do not handle until all safety precautions have been read and understood' for unstable explosives (C.4.14) in favor of a shorter, more relevant instruction to obtain special instructions before use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: 'obtain special instructions before use' is shorter and more relevant; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit subjecting explosives to grinding/shock/friction (conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the precautionary statement 'Do not subject to grinding/shock/friction/. . .' to unstable explosives (C.4.14) and explanatory conditional note clarifying application only if the explosive is mechanically sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement already exists for other explosives categories; adding conditional note ensures it's applied only when mechanically sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require listing of ignition sources (expanded phrasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise ignition-source instruction to 'Keep away from heat, hot surfaces, sparks, open flames, and other ignition sources.' and require label preparers to list applicable ignition sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change consistent with Rev. 7; improves hazard communication by increasing worker awareness of possible ignition sources. OSHA finalized despite industry objections and allowed not relabeling containers already released for shipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'Keep wetted with...' per Rev.7 clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify conditional instruction for 'Keep wetted with . . .' to apply to 'substances or mixtures which are wetted, diluted, dissolved or suspended with a phlegmatizer to reduce or suppress their explosive properties' for Divisions 1.1-1.3 and 1.5 explosives (C.4.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to desensitized explosives as appropriate; aligns with Rev. 7 wording about phlegmatizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'packaging' rather than 'container' where inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 'Keep only in original container' to 'Keep only in original packaging' for certain hazard classes (self-reactive substances C.4.21, organic peroxides C.4.28, corrosive to metals C.4.29, and explosives C.4.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: 'packaging' is more inclusive and covers transport packaging as well as immediate container; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'Ground and bond' instead of 'Ground/bond' where both are required
rubrics_metrics.description: Change 'Ground/bond container and receiving equipment' to 'Ground and bond container and receiving equipment' for electrostatically sensitive chemicals (e.g., explosives C.4.14, flammable liquids C.4.19, flammable solids C.4.20) and add conditional notes clarifying applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where both grounding and bonding are necessary to protect against electrostatic hazards, both words must appear; conditional instructions clarify when grounding/bonding apply (e.g., only if volatile or electrostatically sensitive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize 'Keep away from clothing and other combustible materials'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace various formulations ('Keep/Store away from clothing/.../combustible materials') with 'Keep away from clothing and other combustible materials' for oxidizing chemicals and remove redundant 'incompatible materials' instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: 'combustible materials' generally covers incompatible materials; 'keep' covers storage and use; reduces duplication and confusion; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove combustible-material statement for non-oxidizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the 'Keep/store away from clothing/.../combustible materials' precautionary statement for self-reactive substances and mixtures (C.4.21) and organic peroxides (C.4.28) because they do not have oxidizing properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classes have alternate storage statements more appropriate to their chemical properties; change aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep valves and fittings free from oil and grease (all valves/fittings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise instruction to 'Keep valves and fittings free from oil and grease' for oxidizing gases (C.4.17) to cover all valves and fittings, not just reduction valves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: oil/grease on any valve/fitting can create hazards; consistent with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wear cold insulating gloves plus face shield or eye protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise refrigerated liquefied gases (C.4.18) precautionary statement from 'cold insulated gloves, a face shield, or eye protection' to 'Wear cold insulating gloves and either face shield or eye protection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that cold-insulating gloves are to be used in addition to either face shield or eye protection; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply 'Keep container tightly closed' with conditional instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Add conditional instruction to 'Keep container tightly closed' to indicate it applies to flammable liquids (C.4.19, categories 1–3) when the liquid is volatile and may generate an explosive atmosphere; also add the precaution to pyrophoric liquids/solids and desensitized explosives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures statement only used where appropriate (volatile/explosive-atmosphere risk) and adds it to classes where avoiding air contact is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorten 'precautions against static discharge' to actionable wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 'Take precautionary measures against static discharge' to 'Take action to prevent static discharge' for flammable liquids (C.4.19, Hazard Categories 1–3) and add a note that it applies if the liquid is volatile and may generate an explosive atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies required action and aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require specific selection in 'Use explosion-proof [...] equipment' statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For flammable liquids (C.4.19) and flammable solids (C.4.20), add square brackets in 'Use explosion-proof [electrical/ventilating/lighting/. . .] equipment.' and a conditional instruction that bracketed text may be used to specify particular equipment as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to prevent SDS/labels from listing the entire line without selecting the specific measures appropriate to the chemical; for liquids, add conditional instruction requiring this when liquid is volatile and may generate an explosive atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use non-sparking tools only under specified conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a conditional instruction to use non-sparking tools for flammable liquids (C.4.19, categories 1–3) only if the liquid is volatile, may generate an explosive atmosphere, and the minimum ignition energy is very low (<0.1 mJ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits applicability to situations where non-sparking tools are truly necessary; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move 'Keep cool' from storage to prevention (with conditional omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-reactive substances and mixtures (C.4.21) and organic peroxides (C.4.28), move 'Keep cool' from storage to prevention columns and add a conditional instruction allowing omission if storage temperatures are included on the label; for self-heating substances (C.4.24) handle similarly with 'Protect from sunlight' moved to storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: ensure appropriate temperatures are highlighted during handling as well as storage; avoid repetition when explicit storage temperatures are provided; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional 'Do not allow contact with air/water' emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the conditional note 'if emphasis of the hazard statement is deemed necessary' to 'Do not allow contact with air' (pyrophoric categories) and 'Do not allow contact with water' (substances that emit flammable gases on contact with water) because hazard phrases already warn of these dangers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label preparers may include the precautionary statement for added emphasis when warranted by the specific chemical; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle and store contents under inert gas, specify alternatives if inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Change 'Handle under inert gas. Protect from moisture' to 'Handle and store contents under inert gas/. . . Protect from moisture' for substances that react with water (C.4.25) and add conditional instructions requiring the preparer to specify appropriate liquid or gas if inert gas is not appropriate; extend similar statements to pyrophoric liquids/solids (C.4.22, C.4.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that pyrophoric/reactive chemicals must be both handled and stored under inert atmospheres and instructs label preparers to specify alternatives (e.g., white phosphorus handled/stored under water) where inert gas is not suitable; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify 'Wear fire resistant or flame retardant clothing'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace 'Wear fire/flame resistant/retardant clothing' with 'Wear fire resistant or flame retardant clothing' for Category 1 oxidizing liquids (C.4.26) and solids (C.4.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies OSHA's intent that users should wear either fire resistant OR flame retardant clothing and avoids ambiguity about word choices; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial reorganizations and clarity improvements in response column
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA made numerous editorial changes to the response column to improve clarity, correct omissions, combine statements, and remove redundancy (e.g., adding 'If on skin' to 'Brush off loose particles from skin').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA will provide a redline version of Appendix C on its website; the discussion in the preamble highlights substantive response-column changes beyond purely editorial tweaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rinse skin with 'water [or shower]' using square brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise rinse instruction to 'Rinse skin with water [or shower]' and add a conditional note indicating bracketed text is to be used where the manufacturer/importer/distributor considers a deluge shower appropriate for the specific chemical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows selection of the most appropriate wording (water vs shower) depending on the chemical's decontamination needs; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select between 'medical advice' or 'medical attention'
rubrics_metrics.description: Require label preparers to select either 'get medical advice' or 'get medical attention' as appropriate rather than using a combined 'advice/attention' phrasing for many health hazards (e.g., C.4.4, C.4.5, C.4.7, C.4.8, C.4.9, C.4.10, C.4.12, C.4.18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: medical attention implies in-person evaluation while medical advice may be remote; specifying which is appropriate conveys important information and aligns more closely with Rev. 7/Rev. 8 improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify inhalation response wording
rubrics_metrics.description: For sensitization—respiratory (C.4.6) and other inhalation hazards, change 'If inhaled: If breathing is difficult, remove person to fresh air and keep comfortable for breathing' to 'If inhaled: Remove person to fresh air and keep comfortable for breathing' (remove 'if breathing is difficult').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing the second conditional reduces confusion from double conditions and aligns statements across hazard classes and with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require 'Take off contaminated clothing and wash it before reuse'
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the previously omitted phrase 'Take off contaminated clothing and' to the precautionary statement for skin sensitization (C.4.7), so it reads to remove contaminated clothing and wash it before reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrects an inadvertent omission present in prior revisions and aligns with Rev. 7 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'If exposed or concerned' for certain hazard classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Change precautionary statement from 'If exposed' to 'If exposed or concerned' for specific target organ toxicity (single exposure) (C.4.11) to align with language used for germ cell mutagenicity, carcinogenicity, and reproductive toxicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains consistency across Appendix C and with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division 1.4 explosives: clarify applicability note and firefighting wording
rubrics_metrics.description: For Division 1.4 explosives (C.4.14), change the instructional note wording to 'except for explosives of division 1.4 (compatibility group S) in transport packaging' for clarity, and replace 'Fight fire with normal precautions from a reasonable distance' with 'Fight fire remotely due to the risk of explosion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No intended change in substantive scope for the note; new firefighting wording specifies explosion risk and is more protective; aligns with Rev. 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change 'Eliminate all ignition sources if safe to do so' to 'In case of leakage, eliminate all ignition sources'
rubrics_metrics.description: For flammable gases (C.4.15), revise the instruction to 'In case of leakage, eliminate all ignition sources' and delete 'if safe to do so' to emphasize prompt action on leaks and because a fire may prevent such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: stresses dangers of flammable gas leaks that can form explosive atmospheres; added to new flammable gas categories; commenters argued for keeping 'if safe to do so' but OSHA finalized the change as proposed.
